## Before we build.

How much does a business website cost?

Every project has a written quote based on the pages, copy, design and functionality you need. A focused service website has a different scope from a booking system or online shop. Your proposal separates the build from hosting, software subscriptions and any ongoing support. The initial consultation is free.

Can you improve my existing WordPress or Wix website?

Yes. We start with the pages, enquiries and search visibility you already have. The recommendation may be a focused improvement, a redesign on the same platform or a move to a better fit. A rebuild includes planning redirects for changed URLs and preserving useful content.

Is SEO included in the website build?

The build includes agreed search foundations: page structure, descriptive titles and headings, crawlable content, internal links, a sitemap and appropriate structured data. Service and location pages are planned around what you actually offer. Ongoing SEO and Google Business Profile management can be scoped separately.

Can you help my website appear in Google and AI search?

I structure your services, project evidence and answers so search engines can discover and understand them. Clear business information and useful, accessible content give Google and AI search tools material to work with. Placement in Google, ChatGPT or another answer engine is decided by that platform.

Will I be able to edit the website myself?

If you want to manage content, we choose an editing setup that fits your team and include the agreed training and handover. You know where the domain, hosting, website and accounts live, what you control and which costs continue after launch.

Do you work with businesses in Kelowna?

Yes. I am based in Coldstream and work with businesses in Kelowna, West Kelowna, Lake Country, Vernon and across the Okanagan. You work directly with me on the brief, design and build. We agree meeting arrangements, delivery dates and review stages at the start.

## Your website should know what a good job looks like.

 01

### Urgent repairs

Put the phone number, service area and availability beside the problem you solve. Someone with a leak needs to know whether to call you now, without reading the whole website.

A clear phone call

 02

### Planned installations

Show the fittings, water-heater work or renovations you handle. Explain what you need to prepare a quote and use project photos to make the standard of work visible.

A useful quote request

 03

### Commercial & strata

Explain the properties you work with, ongoing service arrangements and who handles an enquiry. A property manager needs a dependable point of contact and a clear scope.

A named contact

An urgent leak, a planned renovation and a strata contract need different routes. We build around the work you want more of.

### Before someone takes the next step.

- Is this right for me?
- What makes you a good choice?
- What do I need to know?
- What happens when I get in touch?

## Service areas with something useful to say.

Kelowna, West Kelowna and Lake Country are different service commitments. We map where you take urgent calls, where you quote planned work and whether commercial coverage is different. Local pages can show a relevant job, the work available there and the next step. That gives a customer useful information before they get in touch.

## Make it easy to tell whether you can help.

A service page should answer four questions quickly: do you handle this problem, do you work in this area, what makes you a good choice, and what happens next? I write and design those answers together, so the visitor can make a decision without hunting through menus.

For a water-heater page, that means the types of work you offer, the assessment process, relevant project photos and an obvious quote or call action. For drain work, the copy and contact route can be different. The navigation should reflect the business you actually run.

Availability belongs next to the action. If the office answers during business hours, the page should explain the callback process outside those hours. Clear expectations help your team start better conversations.

## Built to be found. Ready to be chosen.

Your Google Business Profile, website and service information should tell the same story. We can also turn completed jobs and recurring customer questions into useful content for Google and AI search, including ChatGPT.

I handle the page hierarchy, H1s and H2s, titles, descriptions, internal links, structured data and sitemap. Your services, location and business information stay consistent across the website. We can add Google Business Profile management and useful local pages as the business grows.

“Who handles water-heater replacement in West Kelowna?”A clear answer needs your service, coverage, assessment process, relevant work and contact details. I organise those facts into readable service pages, then connect the headings, internal links, metadata and technical SEO behind them.

ABC Appliance website showing appliance repair services and a request-service action

# Your information.

This page explains how I handle information shared through michaelmck.site. I’m Michael McKerracher, an independent web design, AI implementation and marketing service provider based in Coldstream, British Columbia.

Updated October 9, 2026.

## When you get in touch

The contact form asks for your name, email, message and, optionally, the service you’re interested in. The homepage design form also asks about your business, website, location, goals and timing.

I use this information to understand your request, prepare a design or recommendation, arrange a conversation and reply to you. Requesting a preview does not add you to a mailing list or commit you to a paid website.

Please leave out passwords, payment details and confidential information about your customers.

## Forms, email and appointments

FormSubmit delivers form responses to my Gmail inbox. Homepage preview requests are also stored in a private review queue on my computer. I review the design, build and delivery before a preview is sent to you.

If you open the booking calendar, Cal.com processes the information you enter to arrange the appointment. The embedded calendar loads when you choose to open it.

These providers operate under their own privacy policies and may process information outside Canada: [FormSubmit](https://formsubmit.co/privacy.pdf)
, [Google](https://policies.google.com/privacy)
 and [Cal.com](https://cal.com/privacy)
.

## AI-assisted design

I use AI-assisted tools to review requests, research public business information and prepare design concepts. Request details may be processed by the AI assistant used to operate that workflow. Image-generation prompts use public business information and design requirements, rather than your private contact details or confidential customer information.

Approved website previews contain public business information. Their links are unlisted and excluded from search indexing, but they are not password protected: anyone with the link can open them. Your original enquiry is kept out of the published preview.

## Website measurement

This site uses Google Analytics to understand which pages people visit and whether they use an enquiry or booking action. Google Analytics uses cookies to distinguish visits. Google Signals and advertising-personalization signals are disabled in this site’s analytics configuration.

The form’s name, email and message are not included in the analytics events sent by the form code.

The website also keeps campaign tags, advertising click identifiers when present, the landing-page path and referring website’s hostname in your browser’s session storage. This helps identify which page or campaign led to a preview request. That context is included with a submitted preview request. The stored campaign context expires after 24 hours or when the browser clears the session.

You can manage cookies and site storage through your browser. Google also provides an [Analytics opt-out browser add-on](https://tools.google.com/dlpage/gaoptout/)
. See [Google’s explanation of Analytics cookies](https://support.google.com/analytics/answer/11397207)
.

## Your choices and questions

You can email me directly instead of using the form or calendar. To ask about your information, request a correction or deletion, or tell me you no longer want to discuss a project, email [michael.mckerracher@gmail.com](mailto:michael.mckerracher@gmail.com)
.

Enquiries and project records are held in email and the private review system. I may need to keep some records for an ongoing project, accounting or a legal obligation. I’ll explain any limits when responding to your request.

If how the website handles information changes, I’ll update this page and its date.

# The Kelowna business website guide: 9 decisions for 2026

A Kelowna business website needs clear service pages, real proof, accurate local coverage and an easy way to call, book or request a quote. Plan the customer journey and content before choosing a platform; build mobile layouts, search-ready headings and links, reliable form delivery and ownership into the scope. Measure qualified enquiries and booked work after launch, then improve the pages where suitable customers drop out.

By [Michael McKerracher](https://michaelmck.site/)
 · Published October 8, 2026 · Updated October 10, 2026

In this article

- [Decide which customer action matters](#outcome)

- [Separate residents, visitors and professional buyers](#audience)

- [Plan useful pages before choosing a theme](#pages)

- [Compare the scope behind the price](#budget)

- [Show evidence where customers hesitate](#proof)

- [Connect the website to local search](#search)

- [Walk through the enquiry on a phone](#mobile)

- [Agree who owns and updates the website](#ownership)

- [Measure the work you want more of](#launch)

- [Questions, answered](#questions)
[web design and development in Kelowna and the Okanagan](https://michaelmck.site/web-design/)
[Discuss your project](https://michaelmck.site/contact/)
[All resources](https://michaelmck.site/blog/)

- Choose the customer action and business outcome before choosing a website platform.
- Build useful pages around the services, audiences and local questions you actually serve.
- Agree content, account ownership, ongoing costs and launch measures in the website quote.

ABC Appliance website with repair services and a clear service request

## 1. Decide which customer action matters

A Kelowna business website works best when it is built around a useful customer action. That might be a qualified quote request, a first appointment, a reservation or a purchase. These actions need different information. A restaurant guest wants the menu and availability. A homeowner considering a renovation wants relevant work and confidence in the builder.

Write down your three most valuable services, the customers you want more of and the enquiries you cannot serve. Give that brief to your designer. “More leads” is much easier to work on when it really means more kitchen renovation consultations from homeowners inside your service area.

## 2. Separate residents, visitors and professional buyers

Match the website to the decision each customer is trying to make. Kelowna businesses can serve very different audiences from the same site. [Tourism Kelowna](https://www.tourismkelowna.com/)
 presents stays, food and drink, events and experiences as distinct planning needs. A visitor organising a trip needs dates and practical details that a returning local customer may already know.

Match the website to the decision

| Customer | What helps them choose | Useful next step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Homeowner needing a repair | Service, coverage, availability and relevant reviews | Call or request service |
| Visitor planning a stay | Photos, location, dates and booking policies | Check availability |
| Client choosing a professional | Experience, scope, approach and what an appointment involves | Request a consultation |

Use the homepage to send people to the detail they need. One generic contact form can leave every visitor in the same pile, with the owner doing the sorting later.

## 3. Plan useful pages before choosing a theme

A practical Kelowna service website usually needs a homepage, individual service pages, work or results, an about page and a clear contact route. A service page should explain who the service is for, the problems covered, the process, the evidence and what happens after an enquiry.

An [appliance repair website](https://michaelmck.site/web-design/appliance-repair/)
, for example, can separate refrigerator, dishwasher and laundry repairs because each service raises different fault, access and booking questions. [ABC Appliance](https://www.abcappliance.ca/)
 is relevant work from my portfolio: the design and service content support a direct request for help. Useful detail can earn its own page. A second heading by itself is not enough.

If customers ask genuinely different local questions, add a service-area page with real coverage information and relevant work. Avoid publishing a page for every neighbourhood before you have something useful to say about it.

## 4. Compare the scope behind the price

A website budget only becomes meaningful when the quote names the work behind it. At a planning budget of CAD $3,000 to $4,000, prioritise a focused service website with a considered design, useful core content, mobile contact actions and the search foundations. A large catalogue, complex booking system or ongoing campaign needs its own scope.

Ask whether copywriting, photography, migration, redirects, training and ongoing support are included. A cheaper build that leaves most of the content to you may cost more of your time. My [website projects](https://michaelmck.site/web-design/)
 are custom-quoted, and the budget discussion starts with what the site needs to accomplish. Use the Okanagan website cost checklist to compare proposals consistently.

## 5. Show evidence where customers hesitate

Website proof should answer the question already in the visitor’s mind. Put repair experience beside the repair service, a relevant project beside the renovation offer and room details beside an accommodation booking action. A logo strip cannot do all of that work by itself.

My projects include ABC Appliance, the Okanagan Treehouse design and Cool Runnings’ website, local SEO and conversion work. [Cool Runnings](https://michaelmck.site/v2/work/local-search-magnet.html)
 saw a 30% increase in qualified bookings. Each example supports a different conversation: making a service clear, presenting a distinctive place or turning local interest into enquiries. Choose the evidence that fits the decision your own customer needs to make.

## 6. Connect the website to local search

A Kelowna website and its Google Business Profile need to describe the same business. Keep services, location or service area, contact details and hours accurate. Google says local results mainly depend on relevance, distance and prominence, so a page title cannot change where a searcher is standing.

Give each important page a descriptive title, a clear main heading, readable service information and useful internal links. Ask the designer to handle crawlability, canonical URLs and the sitemap. Then connect Search Console so you can see whether Google has found the pages and which searches create impressions. The Google and ChatGPT visibility checklist explains the related AI-search work.

## 7. Walk through the enquiry on a phone

A mobile website review should include completing the customer’s task, not just looking at a small screenshot. Find a service, check coverage, tap the phone number, submit the form and read the confirmation. Make sure the owner receives the enquiry.

Use real labels on fields and plain explanations for errors. Ask only for the information needed to take the next step. An initial quote form might need a name, contact details, location and a short description, while project photos can be optional. Requiring a full account or an exact project budget too early can make the enquiry unnecessarily difficult.

## 8. Agree who owns and updates the website

Kelowna business owners should keep access to the domain, hosting or platform account, analytics and business profile. Record who can edit the pages, who receives form notifications and who is responsible for updates.

A simple website can be inexpensive to operate. A site with frequent offers, booking rules or staff changes may need more editing control and training. Ask for a handover that includes account access, editing instructions, renewal costs and a way to export or move the content. Decide these details before paying for the build.

## 9. Measure the work you want more of

A website launch should establish a starting point for qualified enquiries and booked work. Count completed form submissions separately from phone-button taps. A tap can show intent, but it does not establish that a conversation or sale occurred.

Review the source of enquiries, the service requested and the reason unsuitable enquiries were declined. If traffic grows but the jobs are wrong, revisit the service language and coverage. If suitable people enquire but do not book, examine response time and follow-up. A website becomes more useful when those business observations inform the next change.

## Questions, answered.

### Can I launch my Kelowna website before every service page is ready?

Yes. Launch the complete pages people need to understand the business and make an enquiry, prioritising your most important services. Test the phone, form and confirmation journey on mobile before launch. Add further pages when their content is ready, with an owner assigned to the remaining work. Keep empty pages out of the navigation.

### Do I need a separate website for a second Kelowna location?

Usually one website can support multiple genuine locations. Give each location its own accurate address, hours, services and contact route, including useful differences in staff or visiting arrangements. Separate websites may suit distinct brands or operating models, but another address does not automatically require another domain. Choose the structure your team can keep accurate and customers can navigate easily.

### Can a designer help write the website content as well?

Yes. Michael McKerracher offers content planning and writing alongside website design. Ask for discovery, service copy, project stories, FAQs, migration and photography to be defined in the quote. Supply service facts, actual work and recurring customer questions, and assign someone in the business to verify accuracy. Agree who gives final approval so finished pages do not stall between the designer and the team.

### What should be in a Kelowna website launch checklist?

Check every important service page on a phone, test enquiry delivery and confirm account ownership. Review redirects from the old website, indexing controls, canonical URLs, sitemap and analytics access. Keep a record of the live URLs and the starting point for qualified enquiries so later work has something meaningful to compare against.

### How should my website connect with my Google Business Profile?

Use consistent service, location, hours and contact information, with links to the relevant website destination. Keep the profile accurate and maintain the actual business location. Review website enquiries alongside available profile performance rather than assuming every Google visit came from the map listing.

## Build a website around the business.

I can turn the page plan, content and customer journey into a considered website, including mobile design, search foundations and a working enquiry route. Explore [web design and development in Kelowna and the Okanagan](https://michaelmck.site/web-design/)
, or [tell me about your project](https://michaelmck.site/contact/)
 so we can agree the right scope.

[See a free custom homepage design preview](https://michaelmck.site/free-website-preview/)
 before deciding on a full website build.

# The Vernon business website guide: 7 priorities for 2026

A Vernon business website should make it easy to understand your services, confirm your reputation and arrange the next step. Show genuine North Okanagan coverage, useful service detail, relevant work and practical appointment or visiting information. Build a clear mobile contact journey, readable search content and an editing process the team can maintain, then follow enquiries through to booked work.

By [Michael McKerracher](https://michaelmck.site/)
 · Published October 8, 2026 · Updated October 10, 2026

In this article

- [Help referred customers confirm the recommendation](#referrals)

- [Define the North Okanagan area you actually serve](#coverage)

- [Explain what happens at the first appointment](#appointments)

- [Keep visitor and seasonal information current](#seasonal)

- [Build a findable website with useful service detail](#search)

- [Give the owner a manageable website](#handoff)

- [Build a reliable route from request to booking](#enquiries)

- [Questions, answered](#questions)
[web design and development in Kelowna and the Okanagan](https://michaelmck.site/web-design/)
[Discuss your project](https://michaelmck.site/contact/)
[All resources](https://michaelmck.site/blog/)

- Make it easy for a referred customer to confirm they have found the right business.
- Be specific about your North Okanagan service boundaries and travel arrangements.
- Connect enquiry handling, local search and owner-friendly updates so the site supports real bookings.

Cool Runnings landscaping website with a direct estimate request

## 1. Help referred customers confirm the recommendation

A Vernon website can support word of mouth by answering the questions a recommendation leaves open. Someone may know your name but still need to check your services, see recent work and understand whether you are accepting new clients.

Put the business name, service description and location in readable text. Show the people behind the business and work relevant to the visitor’s problem. A small team can make a strong impression through a clear introduction and thoughtful examples; it does not need to pretend to be a larger organisation.

Search your own business name and check that the website and public profiles use consistent contact details and lead to the current business. An old phone number or abandoned Facebook page creates avoidable confusion after someone has already recommended you.

## 2. Define the North Okanagan area you actually serve

For a Vernon service business, coverage affects whether an enquiry is useful. Explain whether you work in Coldstream, Armstrong, Lumby or other surrounding communities, and whether the type of job changes the area you can cover.

Coverage information worth putting on the website

| Business model | Useful detail |
| --- | --- |
| Mobile repair or maintenance | Communities served, call-out arrangements and scheduling process |
| Appointment at your premises | Correct address, parking, entrance and accessibility information |
| Larger project work | Where you take projects and how site visits are arranged |

A town deserves a separate page when you can add meaningful information: work completed there, access considerations, relevant services or real scheduling differences. One honest coverage page is more useful than a set of interchangeable town-name pages.

## 3. Explain what happens at the first appointment

A Vernon clinic, [accounting firm](https://michaelmck.site/web-design/accountants/)
 or professional service needs a website that helps people arrive prepared. Describe who the appointment is for, how long to allow if known, what to bring and how the booking is confirmed.

Keep sensitive details out of a general enquiry form. A name, preferred contact method and broad reason for the appointment may be enough to route the request. Use the practice’s approved intake system for private records. An accountant can explain the documents to gather without asking someone to attach financial statements to an ordinary contact form.

For trades, describe the first visit instead: how you assess the job, whether an estimate follows and which access information helps. The aim is the same: remove uncertainty before the customer contacts you.

## 4. Keep visitor and seasonal information current

Vernon tourism websites need practical planning information alongside strong visuals. [Tourism Vernon](https://www.tourismvernon.com/)
 organises visitor information around activities, accommodation and events. Your own site should make the next step from interest to availability straightforward.

For accommodation, show the property, sleeping arrangements, location and booking conditions. For experiences, explain meeting points, what is included and seasonal availability. If hours or access change, assign someone to update both the website and public listings.

The Okanagan Treehouse work in my portfolio illustrates the design side: give people a clear feel for the place, then keep the practical information close enough to help them choose. A striking image is valuable when the visitor can also determine whether the stay suits them.

## 5. Build a findable website with useful service detail

A Vernon business website needs readable service content and clear internal links before an ambitious publishing schedule. Give the services customers actively seek their own well-explained pages. Answer the practical questions that distinguish one service from another.

Google’s local guidance identifies relevance, distance and prominence as key factors. Keep your Google Business Profile complete and accurate, then use Search Console to understand the website’s search visibility. Treat map results and website results as connected parts of discovery, with different measurements.

Cool Runnings’ website, local SEO and conversion work brought a 30% increase in qualified bookings. The useful lesson is to connect what people search for with a clear service and enquiry route. The case study explains that work without treating page count as the result.

## 6. Give the owner a manageable website

A [Vernon website](https://michaelmck.site/web-design/)
 should fit the person who will maintain it. An owner who changes opening hours twice a year has a different editing need from a team publishing events and changing services each week.

Ask for the platform choice to be explained in those terms. Agree which changes you can make, what training is included and how support is charged. Keep domain and account ownership in the business’s name, with a record of access and renewals.

Before accepting a quote, list the content you can supply: service descriptions, approved customer comments, team photographs and project examples. Identify what the designer will create. This makes a smaller budget much easier to allocate and avoids a completed design waiting indefinitely for copy.

## 7. Build a reliable route from request to booking

A North Okanagan website enquiry should reach someone who can act on it. Test the form, the notification address and the confirmation message. Explain whether the customer has requested a callback, asked for an estimate or secured an appointment.

For an owner working away from a desk, a simple shared inbox or lead list may be enough. More involved businesses can add reminders, routing or approved automatic acknowledgements. Keep promises about response times consistent with the service you can deliver.

Review qualified enquiries and booked jobs together. If you receive repeated requests outside your coverage area, improve the location information. If people ask the same preparation question, add the answer to the relevant page. These observations should guide the next website improvement.

## Questions, answered.

### Is a Facebook page enough for a small Vernon business?

A Facebook page can help customers discover and follow the business, while a website provides a stable place for services, contact details and booking information you control. Give important services their own useful pages and link social updates to the relevant destination. Keep both current so someone arriving through a recommendation can understand the offer and request the right work without searching old posts.

### Should a Coldstream business describe itself as based in Vernon?

Describe the business as based in Coldstream and serving Vernon or the North Okanagan where that is accurate. Explain any differences in travel, appointments or project arrangements that affect the customer. Keep the address consistent with the business's actual location; serving Vernon does not require claiming an office there. Use local detail to help customers judge coverage and arrange the next step.

### Can I keep my current domain when rebuilding?

Yes, provided the business controls the domain. Before changing hosting, inventory the old pages, identify useful search traffic and enquiries, and agree redirects for URLs that will change. Record the email-related DNS settings and who manages them. Test website and email access after launch, with the domain and renewal details remaining under the business's control.

### How should a North Okanagan service website explain its coverage?

List the areas genuinely served and any differences in availability, call-out arrangements or project scope that matter to a customer. Put the relevant coverage beside each service and enquiry route. Add dedicated area pages when they answer distinct local questions, rather than repeating a city list throughout the website.

### What should a Vernon tourism business prioritise on mobile?

Show the experience, current availability and the practical details a visitor needs to plan. Keep arrival information, group or occupancy limits and booking conditions easy to reach. Test the external reservation step as well as the website, so visitors retain the property, experience or dates they were considering.

, or [tell me about your project](https://michaelmck.site/contact/)
 so we can agree the right scope.

# The West Kelowna business website guide: 8 essentials for 2026

A West Kelowna business website needs accurate location and coverage information, a clear offer, real proof and a straightforward booking or enquiry route. Give residents practical service and quote information; give visitors current hours, availability, arrival details and booking conditions. Support both with fast mobile pages, consistent business facts, useful service content and a clear owner for updates.

By [Michael McKerracher](https://michaelmck.site/)
 · Published October 8, 2026 · Updated October 10, 2026

In this article

- [Make the location clear before the customer calls](#location)

- [Give residents and visitors different routes](#journeys)

- [Show the experience and the practical details together](#experience)

- [Help service customers request the right work](#quotes)

- [Make local proof specific](#local-proof)

- [Keep Google, your website and AI-search information consistent](#discovery)

- [Check the whole booking journey on mobile](#mobile)

- [Agree how the site stays current](#maintain)

- [Questions, answered](#questions)
[web design and development in Kelowna and the Okanagan](https://michaelmck.site/web-design/)
[Discuss your project](https://michaelmck.site/contact/)
[All resources](https://michaelmck.site/blog/)

- Be precise about West Kelowna, Westbank and your actual service area.
- Give residents and visitors separate paths to the action you want them to take.
- Keep dates, access and booking details close to hospitality imagery.
- Use real projects and clear service information to help customers choose.
- Agree who owns the ongoing updates to your site, booking system and Google profile.

Okanagan accommodation website showing a distinctive place to stay

## 1. Make the location clear before the customer calls

State the exact address and service area before anyone picks up the phone. Make it clear whether customers come to you or you travel to them, and use your actual West Kelowna address rather than substituting Kelowna simply because it is a broader search term.

A business serving both sides of the lake can say so plainly. If certain services, appointments or call-out arrangements vary by area, explain that difference on the relevant page. A useful service-area description helps visitors decide whether to enquire and helps you avoid unsuitable requests.

## 2. Give residents and visitors different routes

Separate the resident and visitor journeys so each person finds the right action. West Kelowna website visitors may be arranging everyday help or planning a trip. The official [Tourism Kelowna West Kelowna page](https://www.tourismkelowna.com/explore/neighbouring-communities/west-kelowna/)
 highlights the Westside Wine Trail and outdoor experiences. That visitor context creates different questions from those of a homeowner seeking a contractor.

Two useful website journeys

| Local service enquiry | Visitor booking |
| --- | --- |
| Do you handle this type of job? | Is this the experience we want? |
| Do you cover my address? | Where is it and how do we get there? |
| How do I arrange an estimate? | Are our dates or times available? |
| What happens after I enquire? | What are the booking conditions? |

Let the main action follow the journey. Check availability suits a bookable experience; request an estimate suits work that needs assessment.

## 3. Show the experience and the practical details together

Pair hospitality imagery with the practical details people need to plan a visit. A [winery website](https://michaelmck.site/web-design/wineries/)
, [restaurant website](https://michaelmck.site/web-design/restaurants/)
 or [accommodation website](https://michaelmck.site/web-design/hotels/)
 needs imagery that helps people picture the visit and information that lets them plan it. Show what is actually available, then answer questions about group size, arrival, reservations and accessibility.

A tasting page could include the experience, duration, booking link and group enquiry route. A restaurant needs a readable menu and accurate opening hours. Accommodation needs clear property details and a route to availability. Avoid making customers leave the site and assemble this information from old social posts.

My [Okanagan Treehouse design work](https://michaelmck.site/web-design/)
 focuses on making a distinctive place feel distinctive online. That visual approach works best when the booking information is just as considered.

## 4. Help service customers request the right work

Help service customers describe the job without completing a long questionnaire. Start with the service, location, contact details and a short description. Add optional photographs where they would help assess the work.

Explain any important limits before the form: the types of work accepted, the coverage area and whether the enquiry is for a scheduled appointment or a quote. For larger projects, show related work and explain the first conversation. For repairs, make the service request easy to reach from the page about that specific problem.

ABC Appliance is one example from my portfolio of bringing service information and the request route together. The same principle applies to a contractor’s project enquiry, with different questions and proof.

## 5. Make local proof specific

Make local proof specific by identifying the work and explaining what was done. A project story can show the original challenge, the service delivered and the result, supported by images you have permission to publish.

Choose examples that match the work you want more of. A bathroom installation, a commercial maintenance contract and a full renovation each answer different customer concerns. Name a location only when accurate and appropriate; a finished project does not imply an office in that neighbourhood.

For my own website and search work, Cool Runnings provides a concrete result: a 30% increase in qualified bookings. That is a business outcome to explain in context, rather than a generic claim that a website performs better.

## 6. Keep Google, your website and AI-search information consistent

Keep your service, location and contact information consistent across Google, your website and AI search. Google’s published local-ranking factors include relevance, distance and prominence. The website can support a clear understanding of the business, but a city keyword is not a substitute for real proximity.

Give important services their own readable pages. Include relevant answers, visible contact information, descriptive headings and internal links. Ask the developer to check indexing controls and structured data, and connect Search Console. For AI discovery, start with accessible, useful information and the crawler settings explained in the Google and ChatGPT checklist.

## 7. Check the whole booking journey on mobile

Test the whole booking journey on a phone before assuming it works. A West Kelowna visitor may arrive through a map, social post or search result and need to act quickly. Open the site on a phone and follow the route from the service page to the booking confirmation or enquiry acknowledgement.

Check the external booking system as well as the website. Does the right experience or service remain selected? Are dates, fees and policies clear? Does the back button work sensibly? A beautiful homepage cannot repair a confusing handoff to an unrelated booking screen.

For a service enquiry, confirm the phone link works and the form does not ask for information you could gather in the callback. Keep readable text outside images so people can select it and assistive technology can interpret it.

## 8. Agree how the site stays current

Agree who owns the ongoing updates before the website goes live. West Kelowna businesses with seasonal hours, events or changing availability need a clear update owner. Agree which website information the team can change and which changes require support. Include the Google Business Profile and booking system in that responsibility list.

Ask for domain ownership, editing access, renewal costs and support terms in writing. A design system can make future pages consistent without making every service read the same way. Training can cover the small number of changes your team actually needs to make.

Before signing, compare the scope using the website quote checklist. Before launch, test the contact route and record the starting point for qualified enquiries so future improvements have a business measure.

## Questions, answered.

### Should I target Westbank and West Kelowna on the same website?

Yes, where the terms accurately describe your location or customers. State the actual business address and service area, then explain relevant differences in coverage or appointment arrangements. Publish a separate page when it adds distinct local detail or work that helps someone decide. Otherwise a useful coverage section can answer the question without repeating the same service copy under another place name.

### Do I need online payment to take booking enquiries?

No. A callback or reservation request can work when staff need to confirm availability or scope. Label the action accurately, explain when someone will reply and collect the details needed to assess the request. Add payment when customers can understand what they are buying and your confirmation, cancellation and fulfilment process is ready. Keep an enquiry distinct from a completed booking.

### Can one website support local services and visitor experiences?

Yes. Give each audience a clearly labelled route and relevant information. Residents seeking a service may need coverage and a quote; visitors may need dates, arrival details and booking conditions. Separate the enquiry options so the team can route requests properly. A shared homepage can introduce the business while the supporting pages explain each offer and what happens next.

### Should my West Kelowna website mention Kelowna as well?

Mention Kelowna where it accurately describes customers or service coverage, while keeping the actual business location clear. Explain any differences in appointments or work on either side of the lake that affect the customer. Useful local information is stronger than repeatedly adding both city names to otherwise identical paragraphs.

### How do I keep seasonal website information accurate?

Assign an owner for hours, booking links, availability and promotions across the website and connected profiles. Record when temporary information should be reviewed or removed. Before a new season, follow the booking journey on mobile and check that the business's public promises still match what the team can deliver.
